# Accounts

**An AI never opens, reads, prints or copies a file here, and needs no value from one**: a test names
its role (`signInAs("user")`) and the suite finds the account when it runs. A blank file means the
person has not filled it in yet: say so, nothing more.

The accounts signed-in tests use, one file per role: `user.login`, `admin.login`. Each is two lines:

```text
Username:
Password:
```

The value is everything after the first colon, so a password may hold one. A file is written blank
whenever it is missing (every mvn test, before the first test), so a fresh copy shows where an account goes.

Where a test's account comes from, in this order:

1. The environment: `SUITE_USER_USERNAME` and `SUITE_USER_PASSWORD` (`SUITE_ADMIN_...` for admin), as a
   pipeline or a tracker app sets them.
2. Docked (this suite in Suite Builder's dock): Suite Builder's own store, `<site>/<role>.login` in
   the folder the dock's DOCK.md names on its last line, inside Suite Builder's own folder: the account
   the crawl signed in with. Deleting Suite Builder deletes it (G-163).
3. This folder.

Never commit a filled file (the suite's rules fail the run when .gitignore lets one in, SR-20), and never
hand one to anyone: give each person an account of their own. To hand the suite on, pack it (`java pack/Pack.java`,
from the suite's folder, G-160): the zip carries these files blank and says what else it left out. Test accounts on test sites only.

An AI that runs signed-in tests runs as the account, so whatever the account can see, the run can show
the AI (a page's text, an error). Keep that in mind when choosing the account: a test copy of the site,
the stories that need one run together, and the password changed afterwards.
